title: API 401 Unauthorized
identifier: HTTP 401 Unauthorized returned on API request
problem: A customer's API request is rejected with an HTTP 401 Unauthorized response, blocking their integration from authenticating.
visual: HTTP 401 Unauthorized returned on API request
Browser dev tools / Postman console showing status code 401
Response body containing "Unauthorized" or "invalid_token"
Customer's integration logs showing repeated failed auth attempts
symptoms: Every API call from the customer's integration fails with 401.
The error appears regardless of which endpoint is called.
Issue may have started suddenly after working previously.
causes: API token has expired.
API token or key was typed/copied incorrectly.
Token was revoked or regenerated on another system.
Authorization header is missing or malformed in the request.
steps: Ask the customer to share the exact request headers (redacting the secret portion).
Confirm the Authorization header is present and correctly formatted (e.g. "Bearer <token>").
Check the token's expiry date in the account's API settings.
Regenerate a new token if expired or revoked.
Ask the customer to update their integration with the new token and retry.
decision: If a freshly generated, correctly formatted token still returns 401, this is not a customer-side credential issue — escalate.
solution: Issue a new valid API token, confirm the customer updates their integration configuration, and confirm a test request succeeds with a 200 response.
escalation: Escalate if a valid, correctly formatted, non-expired token still returns 401 after regeneration.

title: API 403 Forbidden
identifier: HTTP 403 Forbidden returned on API request
problem: A customer's API request authenticates successfully but is rejected with HTTP 403 Forbidden when accessing a specific resource or endpoint.
visual: HTTP 403 Forbidden returned on API request
Status code 403 in the response
Response body mentioning "insufficient_scope", "forbidden", or "access_denied"
Customer screenshot showing the request succeeds for one endpoint but fails for another
symptoms: Authentication succeeds (not a 401), but the specific action is denied.
Other endpoints using the same token work correctly.
Error may be limited to one resource type or one account feature.
causes: The API token's scope does not include the requested permission.
The account's subscription plan does not include that API feature.
IP-based allowlisting is blocking the request's origin.
The requested resource belongs to a different account or workspace.
steps: Identify exactly which endpoint/resource is returning 403.
Check the token's assigned scopes against what the endpoint requires.
Confirm the account's plan includes this API feature.
Check whether IP allowlisting is enabled and whether the request origin is included.
Confirm the resource ID belongs to the correct account.
decision: If scope, plan, and allowlist are all confirmed correct but 403 persists, escalate for a permissions-engine level investigation.
solution: Reissue a token with the correct scope, add the missing IP to the allowlist, or clarify the plan limitation to the customer, then confirm the request succeeds.
escalation: Escalate if all visible permission settings are correct and the endpoint still returns 403.

title: API 500 Internal Server Error
identifier: HTTP 500 Internal Server Error returned on API request
problem: A customer's well-formed, authenticated API request fails with an HTTP 500 Internal Server Error on the server side.
visual: HTTP 500 Internal Server Error returned on API request
Status code 500 with a generic error body ("Internal Server Error")
Server-side log/stack trace screenshot shared by the customer's developer
No specific field-level error message shown to the customer
symptoms: The request is valid and authenticated but still fails.
Error may be consistent for a specific payload or intermittent under load.
No actionable error detail is returned to the client.
causes: An unhandled exception occurred while processing the request.
A downstream dependency (database, queue, third-party service) is unavailable.
The specific payload triggers an edge case not handled by the API.
A recent deployment introduced a regression.
steps: Capture the exact request payload, endpoint, and timestamp of the failure.
Check backend error logs for the matching stack trace at that timestamp.
Check whether a deployment occurred shortly before the errors began.
Test the same request with a minimal/simplified payload to isolate the trigger field.
Check the health of downstream dependencies the endpoint relies on.
decision: 500 errors are server-side by definition — if the payload is valid, this cannot be resolved by the customer and must go to engineering.
solution: If tied to a recent deployment, roll back or hotfix the regression. If caused by a downstream outage, resolve the dependency and confirm the request now succeeds.
escalation: Always escalate unexplained 500 errors immediately — do not attempt further customer-side troubleshooting.

title: API Timeout
identifier: API request times out with no response (ETIMEDOUT / 504 Gateway Timeout)
problem: A customer's API requests take too long to respond and eventually fail with a connection or gateway timeout.
visual: API request times out with no response (ETIMEDOUT / 504 Gateway Timeout)
Client-side timeout error (e.g. "ETIMEDOUT", "Gateway Timeout 504")
Long "pending" state visible in browser network tab before failure
Customer's integration logs showing elapsed time far above normal response time
symptoms: Requests hang for an extended period before failing.
No response body is returned, only a timeout error.
May be intermittent or consistent for a specific endpoint or payload size.
causes: Network latency or an unstable connection on the customer's side.
The endpoint's server-side processing exceeds the client's timeout limit.
An unusually large or complex request payload is slowing processing.
A firewall or proxy on the customer's network is delaying the connection.
steps: Confirm the customer's network connectivity is stable and consistent.
Check server-side response time metrics for the affected endpoint.
Ask whether the payload is unusually large; suggest batching into smaller requests.
Confirm no firewall/proxy on the customer's side is interfering with the connection.
Retest the same request from a different network to isolate the source.
decision: If server response times are confirmed slow independent of the customer's network, this needs backend optimization rather than a client-side fix.
solution: Optimize the slow endpoint or guide the customer to reduce request size/batch their calls, then confirm requests complete within the expected time.
escalation: Escalate if backend response times are confirmed abnormally slow and require performance investigation.
related: COMP-006 (Application Becomes Slow for Multiple Users)

title: Third-Party Integration Failure
identifier: Third-party integration shows "Disconnected" or stops syncing data
problem: A customer's connected third-party service (CRM, payment processor, messaging tool, etc.) stops exchanging data correctly with the platform.
visual: Third-party integration shows "Disconnected" or stops syncing data
Integration status shown as "Disconnected" or "Error" in account settings
Third-party provider's own error/status page showing an outage
Sync log showing failed jobs with a specific error code
symptoms: Data stops flowing between the platform and the third-party tool.
Integration status indicator shows an error or disconnected state.
Issue may have started after either side updated their API version.
causes: Third-party API credentials expired or were rotated.
The third-party provider changed their API version or deprecated an endpoint.
The third-party service itself is experiencing an outage.
Field mapping between the two systems no longer matches after a schema change.
steps: Check the integration's connection status in account settings.
Confirm whether the third-party provider has a known outage (check their status page).
Verify the stored credentials/API keys for the integration are still valid.
Compare current field mappings against the third-party's latest API documentation.
Reconnect/re-authenticate the integration and run a manual test sync.
decision: If the third-party service confirms an outage on their end, this is outside our control — communicate the outage and monitor for resolution rather than escalating internally.
solution: Refresh expired credentials, update field mappings to match the current API version, and confirm a manual sync completes successfully.
escalation: Escalate internally if credentials and mappings are correct and the third-party has no reported outage, indicating our integration code needs review.

title: Dashboard Error
identifier: Dashboard shows an error message or widgets fail to load
problem: A customer's dashboard fails to load correctly, showing an error message or missing widgets instead of their expected data view.
visual: Dashboard shows an error message or widgets fail to load
Error banner or toast message on the dashboard screen
One or more widgets showing a broken/error icon while others load fine
Browser console showing a failed network request (red entry) tied to a dashboard widget
symptoms: Dashboard shows a visible error message or partial content.
Some widgets load normally while others fail or spin indefinitely.
Issue may be isolated to one customer or affect several simultaneously.
causes: A specific widget's backing data query is failing.
Stale cached frontend assets after a recent release.
A backend service powering dashboard data is degraded.
The customer's dataset is too large for a widget to render within its timeout.
steps: Ask the customer to hard-refresh (clear cache) and reload the dashboard.
Identify exactly which widget(s) are failing versus loading normally.
Check the health of the backend service powering the failing widget's data.
Check browser console for a specific error tied to the failing widget.
If related to data volume, suggest narrowing the widget's date range/filter.
decision: If only one customer is affected and a hard refresh does not fix it, investigate their specific dataset size or filter configuration before escalating.
solution: If caused by a degraded backend service, restore the service. If caused by stale cache, the hard refresh resolves it. Confirm the dashboard now loads fully.
escalation: Escalate if a backend data service is confirmed degraded, or if the issue affects multiple customers simultaneously.

title: Page Not Loading
identifier: A specific page loads blank or shows a browser-level error
problem: A specific page within the application fails to load, showing a blank screen, a browser-level error, or an infinite loading state.
visual: A specific page loads blank or shows a browser-level error
Blank white page with no visible content
Browser "This site can't be reached" or 404-style error
Loading spinner that never resolves, captured in a screen recording or screenshot
symptoms: The page fails to render any content.
Issue is isolated to one specific page while the rest of the app works.
Browser console may show failed asset or script load errors.
causes: A required frontend asset (script or stylesheet) failed to load.
The page's backing API call is failing or timing out.
A routing/navigation misconfiguration specific to that page.
A browser extension or ad-blocker is blocking a required resource.
steps: Confirm the exact URL/page that fails to load.
Check the browser console for failed asset or script errors.
Test whether the page's backing API call succeeds independently (e.g. via direct request).
Ask the customer to disable browser extensions and retry.
Try loading the page in an incognito/private window to rule out local cache issues.
decision: If the page fails consistently across multiple browsers, devices, and a private window, the cause is server-side, not client-side.
solution: If a required asset failed to deploy, fix the CDN/deployment issue. If caused by a browser extension, advise the customer to disable it for this site.
escalation: Escalate if the page fails to load consistently across multiple browsers and devices after ruling out client-side causes.

title: Feature Not Working
identifier: Clicking/using a feature produces no visible result
problem: A specific feature does not perform its intended function when the customer attempts to use it, even though the rest of the application works normally.
visual: Clicking/using a feature produces no visible result
Customer screen recording/screenshot showing a button click with no visible result
Feature area showing an empty state where output should appear
No error message shown at all, just missing expected behavior
symptoms: Customer clicks or triggers the feature and nothing happens.
The feature runs but produces no visible output or result.
The feature worked previously and stopped functioning recently.
causes: A recent code change introduced a regression in that feature.
The feature depends on a backend service that is currently degraded.
The customer's account or plan does not fully support this feature.
A required precondition (e.g., missing data setup) prevents the feature from working.
steps: Confirm exactly what the customer expects the feature to do.
Attempt to reproduce the issue using the same steps the customer describes.
Check whether the feature depends on a currently degraded backend service.
Confirm the customer's account/plan fully supports this feature.
Check for recent deployments that coincide with when the feature broke.
decision: If reproducible and tied to a recent deployment, this is a regression requiring an engineering fix — do not attempt further workarounds.
solution: If tied to a deployment, roll back or patch the regression. If a precondition was missing, guide the customer through correct setup, then confirm the feature works.
escalation: Escalate if the feature is reproducibly broken and traced to a recent code change.
related: COMP-014 (Feature Stops Working After Product Update)

title: Application Crash
identifier: Application closes or reloads unexpectedly (crash)
problem: The web or mobile application closes, reloads, or becomes unresponsive unexpectedly during normal use.
visual: Application closes or reloads unexpectedly (crash)
Mobile OS crash dialog ("App has stopped")
Browser tab crash screen ("Aw, snap!" or similar)
Customer-shared crash log or stack trace file
symptoms: Application closes or reloads unexpectedly without warning.
Crash may be tied to a specific action (e.g., opening a certain screen).
Crash logs are generated on mobile devices at the time of the incident.
causes: An unhandled exception occurred in the application code.
Insufficient device memory when processing a large dataset.
The customer is on an outdated app version with a known, already-fixed bug.
Corrupted local cache or app data on the customer's device.
steps: Identify the exact action that triggers the crash, if reproducible.
Confirm which app version and device/OS the customer is using.
Check whether the customer is on the latest available app version.
Ask the customer to clear the app's local cache/data and retry.
Collect the crash log or stack trace if available for engineering review.
decision: If the crash is reproducible on the latest app version and is not resolved by clearing local data, this is a code-level defect.
solution: If outdated, guide the customer to update the app. If caused by corrupted local data, clearing the cache resolves it.
escalation: Escalate if the crash is reproducible on the current app version and unresolved by clearing local data.

title: Data Display Error
identifier: Displayed data on screen does not match the underlying stored data
problem: The application shows incorrect, outdated, or garbled data on screen even though the underlying data is correct in the system.
visual: Displayed data on screen does not match the underlying stored data
Screenshot showing obviously wrong values (e.g., negative counts, garbled characters, misaligned columns)
Side-by-side comparison of displayed value vs. the customer's own record
Console error tied to a rendering or formatting function
symptoms: Values on screen do not match the customer's own records.
Data appears in the wrong format (currency, date, encoding).
Issue is a display/rendering problem, not a data loss problem.
causes: A frontend rendering or formatting bug affecting how data is displayed.
Stale cached data being shown instead of the current value.
A locale/regional formatting mismatch (date, currency, number format).
A display-layer bug introduced in a recent release.
steps: Confirm the underlying data is correct by checking it directly in the backend/admin view.
Ask the customer to hard-refresh to rule out stale cached data.
Check the customer's locale/region settings against the expected format.
Reproduce the display issue on a test account to confirm it is not account-specific.
Check recent release notes for known display-layer changes.
decision: If the underlying data is correct but the display remains wrong after a refresh, this is a rendering bug, not a data problem.
solution: Fix the formatting/rendering logic or correct the locale setting, then confirm the customer sees accurate data after a refresh.
escalation: Escalate if the underlying data is verified correct but the UI consistently displays it incorrectly.

title: Login Failure
identifier: Login rejected with "Invalid credentials" or "Login failed"
problem: A customer is unable to log in to their account despite entering what they believe are correct credentials.
visual: Login rejected with "Invalid credentials" or "Login failed"
Login form showing "Invalid email or password" in red text
Repeated failed login attempts visible in the account's security log
Screenshot of a CAPTCHA or lockout notice appearing after several attempts
symptoms: Login page rejects the customer's email and password combination.
Error message states 'Invalid credentials' or 'Login failed'.
May affect a single user or several users on the same account.
causes: Incorrect password entered by the user.
Account is locked after repeated failed login attempts.
The authentication service (SSO/OAuth provider) is degraded.
Account is disabled, suspended, or has an expired invitation.
steps: Verify the account status: active, locked, or disabled.
Check the authentication service status page for ongoing incidents.
If locked, guide the customer through the self-service unlock or reset flow.
If SSO-related, confirm the identity provider (IdP) connection is active.
Confirm the customer is using the correct account/tenant if multiple exist.
decision: If the account is active, unlocked, and SSO is healthy, but login still fails, treat this as an authentication-service issue rather than a user error.
solution: Unlock the account and confirm login succeeds after a fresh password reset, or restore the SSO connection if that was degraded.
escalation: Escalate if root cause cannot be isolated after all steps, or if the SSO/IdP integration itself appears broken for multiple users.

title: Password Reset Failure
identifier: Password reset link is invalid/expired, or reset email never arrives
problem: A customer attempts to reset their password but the process fails, or the reset email never arrives.
visual: Password reset link is invalid/expired, or reset email never arrives
Empty inbox/spam folder screenshot from the customer
"This link has expired or already been used" error page
Password field showing a rejected/complexity error after entering a new password
symptoms: Customer requests a password reset but receives no email.
Reset link returns an 'invalid or expired link' error.
New password is rejected as invalid immediately after reset.
causes: Reset email delivery is delayed or blocked by a spam filter.
Reset link has expired (typically valid for a limited time window).
Reset link was already used once and cannot be reused.
The new password does not meet the platform's complexity requirements.
steps: Confirm the customer's email address on file is correct and active.
Ask the customer to check spam/junk folders for the reset email.
Confirm the reset link is being used within its valid time window.
If expired, trigger a new reset email from the account.
Confirm the new password meets the platform's complexity rules.
decision: If a fresh reset link (used promptly) still fails, this points to an email delivery or token-generation problem, not user error.
solution: Trigger a new password reset email and confirm the customer completes the flow within the valid time window using a compliant password.
escalation: Escalate if reset emails are not being delivered to multiple customers, which may indicate an email delivery service outage.

title: Session Expiration
identifier: User is logged out unexpectedly with a "Session expired" message
problem: A customer is unexpectedly logged out of the application while actively using it, well before any expected timeout.
visual: User is logged out unexpectedly with a "Session expired" message
Sudden redirect to login screen mid-action, captured in a screen recording
"Session expired, please log in again" toast/banner
Browser dev tools showing the auth token cookie missing or invalidated
symptoms: Customer is redirected to the login page mid-session with no warning.
Message displayed: 'Session expired' or 'Please log in again'.
Occurs repeatedly, sometimes within minutes of logging in.
causes: Session token expired earlier than expected due to a configuration issue.
The token refresh mechanism is failing silently in the background.
Customer has multiple tabs/devices open, causing session conflicts.
System clock mismatch between client and server affecting token validity.
steps: Confirm how frequently the session is expiring and under what conditions.
Check whether the token refresh service is functioning correctly.
Ask the customer to close duplicate tabs or sign out of other devices.
Verify the customer's device clock is set correctly and synced.
Have the customer fully log out and back in to establish a clean session.
decision: If expiration happens well below the configured timeout and is not explained by client-side factors, treat this as a token-refresh defect.
solution: Restore the token refresh mechanism if it was failing, or advise the customer to use a single active session if conflicts were the cause.
escalation: Escalate if sessions expire well below the configured timeout and cannot be traced to a client-side cause.

title: Permission Denied
identifier: "Permission denied" or "You do not have access" error on a specific feature
problem: A customer can log in successfully but is blocked from accessing a specific feature, page, or data set they expect to have access to.
visual: "Permission denied" or "You do not have access" error on a specific feature
"You do not have permission to view this page" error screen
Feature/menu item visibly missing compared to a screenshot from before
Admin panel screenshot showing the user's current role/permission set
symptoms: Error message: 'Permission denied' or 'You do not have access to this resource'.
The feature or menu item is missing entirely from the customer's view.
Access worked previously and stopped after a role or plan change.
causes: The customer's user role does not include the required permission.
The account's subscription plan does not include the requested feature.
A permission was recently changed or revoked by an account administrator.
A caching issue is showing outdated permission data.
steps: Confirm the customer's assigned role and its associated permissions.
Confirm the account's current subscription plan includes the feature.
Check the account's permission change history for recent updates.
Ask the customer to log out and back in to refresh cached permission data.
If permissions look correct but access still fails, check for a caching/sync delay.
decision: If the role and plan clearly should grant access but the system still denies it after a fresh login, this is a permission-evaluation bug.
solution: Update the role or plan as appropriate (with administrator approval), or resolve the caching issue with a fresh login, then confirm access.
escalation: Escalate if the role and plan clearly should grant access but the system still denies it after a fresh login.

title: SSO Authentication Failure
identifier: SSO login fails or redirect loop occurs at the identity provider
problem: A customer using Single Sign-On (SSO) is unable to authenticate into the platform through their organization's identity provider.
visual: SSO login fails or redirect loop occurs at the identity provider
Identity provider's own error page (e.g. "AADSTS..." Azure AD error code)
Redirect loop between the platform login and the IdP login screen
"SSO configuration error" message on the platform's login page
symptoms: Customer is redirected to their IdP but the login does not complete.
An error code specific to the IdP is displayed (e.g., SAML or OAuth error).
May affect all users of an organization or only specific ones.
causes: The SSO/SAML configuration between the platform and the IdP is misconfigured.
SSL certificate used for the SSO connection has expired.
The specific user is not provisioned or assigned correctly in the IdP.
The identity provider itself is experiencing an outage.
steps: Confirm whether the issue affects all users of the organization or just one.
Check the SSO configuration's certificate expiry date.
Verify the affected user's provisioning status in the IdP.
Check the identity provider's own status page for ongoing incidents.
Review the exact IdP error code returned, if any, for a specific cause.
decision: If it affects only one user, focus on their IdP provisioning; if it affects the whole organization, focus on the SSO configuration/certificate.
solution: Renew the expired certificate, correct the SSO configuration, or provision the affected user correctly in the IdP, then confirm login succeeds.
escalation: Escalate if the SSO configuration is confirmed correct but authentication still fails for the organization.
related: COMP-007 (SSO Works for Some Users but Not Others)

title: Payment Failure
identifier: Payment attempt is declined or fails at checkout
problem: A customer's payment attempt (subscription charge or one-time purchase) fails to process successfully.
visual: Payment attempt is declined or fails at checkout
Checkout screen showing "Payment declined" or "Card was not approved"
Payment gateway error code shown to the customer or in logs
Bank/card statement showing a declined authorization attempt
symptoms: Payment attempt returns a decline or failure message.
Customer's card may have worked previously for other charges.
Failure may be immediate or occur after a processing delay.
causes: Card has expired or has insufficient funds.
The payment gateway is experiencing a temporary outage.
The card issuer's fraud detection is blocking the transaction.
Billing address or CVV does not match the card on file.
steps: Check the exact decline reason returned by the payment gateway.
Confirm the card's expiry date and billing details match what's on file.
Check the payment gateway's status page for ongoing incidents.
Ask the customer to try an alternate payment method to isolate the cause.
If a fraud-block is suspected, advise the customer to contact their card issuer.
decision: A specific decline code (insufficient funds, expired card) points to the customer's bank; a generic gateway error points to our payment processor.
solution: Guide the customer to update their card details or try an alternate payment method, then confirm the retry succeeds.
escalation: Escalate if the payment gateway itself is confirmed degraded and affecting multiple customers.
related: BILL-002 (Payment Successful but Access Not Updated)
COMP-011 (Payment Successful but Subscription Webhook Fails)

title: Payment Successful but Access Not Updated
identifier: Payment succeeded on the card/bank statement but account access/plan is unchanged
problem: A customer's payment is confirmed as successful, but their account does not reflect the upgraded plan or restored access.
visual: Payment succeeded on the card/bank statement but account access/plan is unchanged
Bank/card statement showing the charge went through
Account page still showing the old/expired plan after payment
Billing history showing 'Paid' status while feature access remains locked
symptoms: Customer confirms the charge appears on their bank/card statement.
Account still shows the old plan or a locked/restricted state.
Feature access has not been unlocked despite successful payment.
causes: The webhook that notifies the platform of a successful payment failed to deliver.
There is a processing delay between payment confirmation and account update.
The payment was applied to the wrong account or subscription ID.
An error occurred in the account provisioning step after payment.
steps: Confirm the payment status directly in the payment gateway's dashboard.
Check whether the corresponding webhook event was received and processed.
Confirm the payment was linked to the correct account/subscription ID.
Manually trigger the account provisioning step if the automated one failed.
Confirm the customer's access reflects the new plan after the manual update.
decision: If the webhook was never received, this is a delivery problem to fix at the integration level, not just a one-off manual correction.
solution: Manually apply the correct plan/access to unblock the customer immediately, and fix the underlying webhook delivery issue to prevent recurrence.
escalation: Escalate if webhook delivery failures are recurring rather than a one-time incident, since this indicates a systemic integration issue.
related: COMP-011 (Payment Successful but Subscription Webhook Fails)

title: Incorrect Invoice
identifier: Invoice shows an amount or line item the customer does not recognize
problem: A customer's invoice shows an amount, plan, or line item that does not match what they expect to be billed.
visual: Invoice shows an amount or line item the customer does not recognize
PDF/screenshot of the invoice with the incorrect line item highlighted
Side-by-side of expected vs. actual charge amount
Account billing history showing a plan change the customer doesn't recognize
symptoms: Customer reports being charged an incorrect amount.
Invoice shows a plan or add-on the customer does not recognize.
Discrepancy appeared after a plan change, upgrade, or renewal.
causes: Proration was calculated incorrectly during a mid-cycle plan change.
An add-on or seat was added but not clearly communicated to the customer.
Currency or tax configuration mismatch for the account's billing region.
A billing system calculation error in a specific edge case.
steps: Pull the account's billing history and compare it against the current invoice.
Check for recent plan changes, upgrades, or added seats/add-ons.
Verify tax and currency settings match the customer's billing region.
If a proration error is confirmed, manually calculate the correct adjustment.
Do not issue any refund or credit without Billing Team approval.
decision: Any invoice correction involving a refund or credit must go through Billing Team approval — never resolve financial adjustments unilaterally.
solution: Once the discrepancy is confirmed and approved, issue the correct invoice adjustment or credit and confirm the customer's next invoice reflects the fix.
escalation: Always escalate to the Billing Team for any refund, credit, or invoice correction, and if the discrepancy pattern affects multiple customers.

title: Email Configuration Failure
identifier: "SMTP authentication failed" when sending outgoing email
problem: A customer cannot send outgoing emails from the platform because their email/SMTP configuration is incorrect.
visual: "SMTP authentication failed" when sending outgoing email
"SMTP authentication failed" error in account settings
Test email send button showing a red failure indicator
Bounce-back message screenshot from the customer's mail server
symptoms: Outgoing emails fail silently or return a bounce/error message.
Feature worked previously and stopped after a settings change.
Error log shows SMTP authentication or connection failure.
causes: Incorrect SMTP host, port, or encryption (TLS/SSL) setting.
Expired or revoked SMTP credentials or API key.
Sending domain is not verified (SPF/DKIM misconfiguration).
The outbound email provider account is suspended or over its sending quota.
steps: Confirm the SMTP host, port, and encryption values in account settings.
Send a test email and capture the exact error returned.
Verify SMTP credentials are current; regenerate the API key if expired.
Check domain verification status (SPF/DKIM) in the email provider console.
Confirm the sending account is active and within its sending quota.
decision: If SMTP settings and domain verification both check out but sending still fails, treat this as a provider-side account issue.
solution: Correct the SMTP settings, verify domain records, and confirm test emails deliver successfully to a real inbox.
escalation: Escalate if domain verification and SMTP settings all appear correct but emails still fail to send.

title: Notification Configuration Failure
identifier: Expected notification is not received despite settings appearing enabled
problem: A customer is not receiving expected in-app, email, or push notifications due to notification settings on their account.
visual: Expected notification is not received despite settings appearing enabled
Notification settings page showing a toggle unexpectedly off
Empty notification center despite a triggering event occurring
Test-notification button producing no result on the customer's device
symptoms: Customer reports missing notifications for events that should trigger them.
Notification settings appear enabled but nothing is received.
Some notification types work while others do not.
causes: The specific notification type is disabled in the customer's preferences.
The notification delivery channel (email/in-app/push) is misconfigured.
Account-level notification settings are overriding user-level preferences.
A recent update reset notification preferences to default.
steps: Confirm which specific notification type is missing.
Check the customer's notification preferences for that type and channel.
Check account-level notification settings for conflicting overrides.
Confirm the delivery channel (email/in-app/push) is correctly enabled.
Trigger a test event and confirm whether the notification is received.
decision: If preferences are enabled at both the user and account level but the notification still doesn't arrive, the issue is in the delivery pipeline, not settings.
solution: Correct the notification preference or delivery channel setting and confirm the customer receives a test notification.
escalation: Escalate if preferences are correctly configured but the notification is still not delivered.

title: User Permission Configuration
identifier: A specific user's role is missing a permission that should be present
problem: An account administrator has configured user roles or permissions in a way that unintentionally blocks legitimate access for one or more users.
visual: A specific user's role is missing a permission that should be present
Admin role-editor screen showing a missing permission checkbox
Comparison screenshot of two users' roles side-by-side
Error message referencing the specific missing permission name
symptoms: A user cannot access a feature the administrator believes they should have.
Multiple users on an account report inconsistent access to the same feature.
Access worked previously and stopped after a role/permission change.
causes: The user's assigned role does not include the required permission.
A custom role was created without the necessary permission included.
Permission inheritance from a parent group/team is misconfigured.
A recent bulk role change was applied incorrectly.
steps: Confirm the specific user's assigned role and its permission set.
Compare against the permissions required for the feature in question.
Check whether a custom role is missing an expected permission.
Review any recent bulk role or permission changes on the account.
Update the role/permission and confirm access is restored.
decision: If the permission structure looks correct on paper but access is still denied, suspect a permission-evaluation defect rather than a configuration mistake.
solution: Update the affected role to include the required permission, or reassign the user to a role that already has it, then confirm access.
escalation: Escalate if the permission structure is correct but access is still denied, which may indicate a permission-evaluation defect.
related: COMP-001 (Feature Works for One User but Not Another)

title: Account Configuration Issue
identifier: An account-level setting (timezone/region/currency) produces wrong downstream behavior
problem: A general account-level setting (timezone, region, default currency, workspace settings) is misconfigured, causing unexpected behavior elsewhere in the platform.
visual: An account-level setting (timezone/region/currency) produces wrong downstream behavior
Account settings page showing an obviously wrong value (e.g. wrong timezone/region)
Downstream effect screenshot (e.g. wrong timestamps caused by the setting)
Settings change history log showing a recent edit
symptoms: A downstream feature (reports, invoices, notifications) behaves incorrectly.
No error message is shown, just unexpected output tied to account settings.
Issue started after an account-level setting was changed.
causes: A setting was changed incorrectly, intentionally or by mistake.
Default configuration was never adjusted for the customer's actual use case.
Two related account settings are in conflict with each other.
A configuration change has not yet propagated/taken effect.
steps: Identify exactly which account setting controls the affected downstream behavior.
Compare the current value against the recommended or default value.
Check the account's configuration change history for recent edits.
Check for conflicting settings that may override each other.
Correct the setting and confirm the downstream behavior returns to normal.
decision: Trace the downstream symptom back to its root account setting before making any change — do not patch the symptom directly.
solution: Correct the misconfigured account-level setting and confirm the downstream feature now behaves as expected.
escalation: Escalate if the setting appears correct but the downstream behavior still does not match documentation.

title: Feature Configuration Issue
identifier: A feature's own settings panel value does not match its actual behavior
problem: A specific feature is set up incorrectly by the customer or an administrator, causing it to behave differently than expected.
visual: A feature's own settings panel value does not match its actual behavior
Feature's own settings panel showing an unexpected value or toggle state
Before/after screenshot showing the feature's behavior changed after a setting edit
Feature configuration change log
symptoms: The feature runs but produces output that doesn't match the customer's setup.
No error message is shown, just a mismatch between configuration and result.
Issue started right after a feature-specific setting was changed.
causes: A feature-specific setting was changed incorrectly.
The feature's default configuration doesn't suit the customer's use case.
A dependency between this feature and another setting was not accounted for.
Cached configuration is serving an outdated value.
steps: Identify the specific feature setting believed to be causing the behavior.
Compare the current configuration against the documented recommended setup.
Check the feature's configuration change history.
Check for a dependent setting elsewhere that could be overriding this one.
Correct the configuration and confirm the feature now behaves as expected.
decision: If the configuration matches documentation exactly but behavior is still wrong, this is a feature-logic bug, not a setup mistake.
solution: Correct the feature-specific configuration value and confirm the feature's output now matches the customer's expectation.
escalation: Escalate if the configuration is confirmed correct per documentation but the feature still behaves incorrectly.

title: Data Synchronization Failure
identifier: Data created/changed in one connected system does not appear in the other
problem: Data fails to sync correctly between two connected systems (e.g., mobile and web, or the platform and a third-party tool).
visual: Data created/changed in one connected system does not appear in the other
Sync status indicator showing "Failed" or a red error icon
Side-by-side screenshot showing data present on one platform but missing on the other
Sync log showing a specific failed job entry
symptoms: Changes made in one system do not appear in the other.
A sync status indicator shows a failed or stalled state.
Issue may be one-directional (only failing one way) or affect both directions.
causes: An expired or invalid authentication token between the two systems.
A network interruption occurred during the sync process.
A schema mismatch between the two systems' data models.
The sync job itself is stuck or has silently failed in the queue.
steps: Check the sync job queue for the customer's stuck or failed job.
Confirm the authentication token between the two systems is still valid.
Check for a recent schema change on either system that could cause a mismatch.
Manually re-trigger the sync job and monitor the result.
Confirm data now matches on both systems after the re-trigger.
decision: A one-time stuck job can be manually re-triggered; a repeatedly failing sync points to a token or schema problem that needs a real fix.
solution: Refresh the expired token, correct the schema mapping, or manually re-trigger the stuck job, then confirm both systems show matching data.
escalation: Escalate if the sync fails repeatedly even after a manual re-trigger and valid credentials.

title: Data Import Failure
identifier: File import fails entirely or specific rows are rejected
problem: A customer attempts to import data (via file upload or integration) and the import process fails or completes with errors.
visual: File import fails entirely or specific rows are rejected
Import summary screen showing "X rows failed" with an error count
Uploaded file screenshot showing a formatting issue (wrong column headers, encoding)
Error log listing specific row numbers that failed
symptoms: Import process fails entirely or completes with partial errors.
Error message references a specific row, column, or field.
Some records import successfully while others are rejected.
causes: The uploaded file's format doesn't match the expected template (wrong columns, headers).
Specific rows contain invalid data types or missing required fields.
The file exceeds the maximum allowed size or row count.
A character encoding mismatch is corrupting special characters.
steps: Review the import error log for the specific rows/fields that failed.
Compare the uploaded file's structure against the required import template.
Check for missing required fields or invalid data types in the failed rows.
Confirm the file size and row count are within platform limits.
Ask the customer to correct the flagged rows and re-attempt the import.
decision: If the file matches the template exactly and specific valid rows still fail, this points to an import-logic bug rather than a file formatting issue.
solution: Guide the customer to correct the file format or flagged rows, then confirm a re-attempted import completes successfully.
escalation: Escalate if correctly formatted, valid data still fails to import.

title: Data Export Failure
identifier: "Export could not be completed" error during data export
problem: A customer attempts to export data out of the platform and the export process fails or produces an incomplete file.
visual: "Export could not be completed" error during data export
"Export could not be completed" error message
Export progress bar stuck or stalled indefinitely
Downloaded file that opens with missing or truncated rows
symptoms: Export button does nothing, or the export fails partway through.
Error message: 'Export could not be completed.'
Issue is reproducible on large exports (e.g., over 10,000 rows).
causes: Export job times out when processing very large datasets.
The background export worker queue is backed up.
The browser is blocking the download pop-up for the exported file.
The requested export format has a known limitation with certain characters.
steps: Confirm the size of the data being exported.
If large, ask the customer to filter the date range or dataset before exporting.
Check the export worker queue for backlog or failed jobs.
Ask the customer to allow pop-ups/downloads for the site.
Manually trigger the export job from the admin console if needed.
decision: If a smaller filtered export succeeds but the full export fails, the issue is a size/timeout limitation, not a data problem.
solution: Guide the customer to export in smaller batches, or clear the export queue backlog, then confirm the export completes.
escalation: Escalate if the export queue is systemically backed up and affecting multiple customers.

title: Duplicate Records
identifier: The same record appears more than once in a list or report
problem: The same record (contact, transaction, item) appears more than once in the customer's data, when it should appear only once.
visual: The same record appears more than once in a list or report
List view showing two visibly identical rows/records
Record IDs shown side-by-side proving they are separate entries with the same data
Sync/import log showing the same source record processed twice
symptoms: Customer sees the same record listed multiple times.
Duplicate records may have identical or near-identical field values.
Issue often appears after a sync, import, or integration event.
causes: A sync or import process ran twice on the same source data.
A pagination bug caused an integration to fetch the same records repeatedly.
No unique-identifier matching rule exists to prevent duplicate creation.
A retry mechanism resubmitted a request that had actually already succeeded.
steps: Confirm how the duplicate records were created (import, sync, manual entry).
Check integration/import logs for repeated processing of the same source record.
Check whether a unique-identifier de-duplication rule exists and is functioning.
Identify and safely merge or remove the duplicate records.
Confirm no data was lost in the merge/removal process.
decision: Never delete a record without confirming which one is the 'source of truth' — merging is safer than deletion when data might differ between duplicates.
solution: Merge or remove the duplicate records after confirming no data loss, and fix the underlying cause (pagination bug, retry logic, missing dedup rule).
escalation: Escalate if duplicates are actively being created on an ongoing basis rather than a one-time historical issue.

title: Missing Records
identifier: An expected record cannot be found anywhere in the platform
problem: A customer expects to see a specific record (contact, transaction, file) in the platform, but it does not appear anywhere.
visual: An expected record cannot be found anywhere in the platform
Search results screenshot showing zero results for a record the customer expects
Filter/view screenshot proving the record isn't hidden by a filter
Source system screenshot proving the record exists there but not on the platform
symptoms: A specific expected record cannot be found anywhere in the platform.
Customer confirms the record exists in the source system (if synced/imported).
May affect a single record or a batch from the same import/sync event.
causes: The record failed silently during an import or sync process.
The record is hidden by an active filter or view setting.
The record was accidentally deleted or archived.
A permissions restriction is hiding the record from this specific user.
steps: Confirm the customer isn't viewing through a filter that would hide the record.
Check the import/sync logs for that specific record around the expected time.
Check whether the record was deleted or archived in the activity log.
Confirm the customer's permissions allow visibility of this record type.
If missing from an import, manually re-import just that record.
decision: Always rule out filters and permissions first — these account for the majority of 'missing' record reports and require no data recovery.
solution: Remove the hiding filter, restore the archived record, adjust permissions, or manually re-import the missing record, then confirm visibility.
escalation: Escalate if the record cannot be located anywhere, including logs, and may indicate actual data loss.

title: Email Notification Not Received
identifier: Expected email notification never arrives (inbox and spam both empty)
problem: A customer expects to receive a specific email notification (alert, confirmation, digest) from the platform, but it never arrives.
visual: Expected email notification never arrives (inbox and spam both empty)
Empty inbox and spam folder screenshot from the customer
Email delivery log showing the message as "sent" but not "delivered"
Notification settings screen showing the relevant toggle enabled
symptoms: Customer confirms the triggering event occurred but no email arrived.
Spam and junk folders have been checked and are empty.
Other email types from the platform may still be arriving normally.
causes: The email was blocked or filtered by the customer's spam filter.
The customer's email address on file is outdated or incorrect.
The notification preference for this specific email type is disabled.
The email delivery service experienced a delay or partial outage.
steps: Confirm the customer's email address on file is correct and active.
Ask the customer to check spam/junk folders thoroughly.
Check the notification preference for this specific email type.
Check the email delivery service's logs for this message's delivery status.
Send a manual test notification to confirm delivery works.
decision: If the delivery log shows the email was sent successfully but never arrived, focus on the customer's spam filter or email provider, not the platform's sending logic.
solution: Correct the email address, enable the notification preference, or resend the notification once delivery is confirmed working.
escalation: Escalate if the email delivery service itself shows failures affecting multiple customers.

title: Report Generation Failure
identifier: Report status stays stuck on "Processing" and never completes
problem: A customer requests a report but it never completes generating, or the process fails outright.
visual: Report status stays stuck on "Processing" and never completes
Report status stuck at "Processing" with a timestamp far in the past
"Report generation failed" error message
Report job queue screenshot showing a stalled or errored job
symptoms: Customer clicks 'Generate Report' and nothing happens after a long wait.
Report status remains stuck at 'Processing' indefinitely.
No error message is shown; the report simply never appears.
causes: The report generation job is stuck or has silently failed in the queue.
The requested date range or dataset is too large to process in time.
A backend reporting service is degraded or unavailable.
A required data source for the report is temporarily unreachable.
steps: Check the report job queue for the customer's stuck or failed request.
Confirm the size of the requested date range/dataset.
Check the health of the backend reporting service.
Ask the customer to retry with a smaller date range as a test.
Manually re-trigger the report generation job if it is confirmed stuck.
decision: If a smaller date range completes successfully, the issue is a size/timeout limitation rather than a service outage.
solution: Manually re-trigger the stuck job, or guide the customer to a smaller date range, then confirm the report completes.
escalation: Escalate if the reporting service itself is degraded and affecting multiple customers.

title: Report Download Failure
identifier: Report finishes generating but the download does not start or completes corrupted
problem: A report finishes generating successfully but the customer cannot download the resulting file.
visual: Report finishes generating but the download does not start or completes corrupted
Download button producing no visible action when clicked
Browser download-blocked notification icon
Partial/corrupted file that fails to open, shown in the customer's file explorer
symptoms: Download button does nothing when clicked.
Download starts but the file is incomplete or corrupted.
Browser blocks the download without any visible reason to the customer.
causes: The browser is blocking the download pop-up or file download.
The generated file link has expired before the customer clicked it.
A network interruption occurred during the file download.
The file storage service is temporarily unavailable.
steps: Ask the customer to allow pop-ups/downloads for the site in browser settings.
Confirm whether the download link has expired; regenerate if needed.
Ask the customer to retry the download on a stable network connection.
Check the file storage service status for any ongoing issues.
Try downloading the same report from an admin/internal account to compare.
decision: If an internal test download succeeds but the customer's fails, the issue is client-side (browser/network), not the file itself.
solution: Regenerate the download link if expired, and confirm the customer can successfully download the file after adjusting browser settings.
escalation: Escalate if downloads are failing for multiple customers, indicating a file storage service issue.

title: Report Export Failure
identifier: Report export to a specific file format (CSV/Excel/PDF) fails
problem: A customer attempts to export a generated report into a specific file format (CSV, Excel, PDF) and the export step fails.
visual: Report export to a specific file format (CSV/Excel/PDF) fails
Format-specific error (e.g. "Could not generate PDF")
Export progress indicator that stalls at a fixed percentage
Corrupted/blank file that fails to open in the target application
symptoms: Export completes for one format but fails for another.
Specific characters or fields seem to break the export.
Issue reproducible for large or specially formatted reports.
causes: The specific export format has a limitation with certain characters or field types.
The report contains more rows/columns than the format supports.
A rendering library issue specific to one export format (e.g., PDF).
The export worker times out for large report exports.
steps: Confirm exactly which export format is failing (CSV, Excel, PDF, etc.).
Check whether specific characters or unusually large fields are present.
Test exporting a smaller version of the same report to isolate the trigger.
Check the export worker's logs for the specific failure at that timestamp.
Try an alternate format as a temporary workaround for the customer.
decision: If only one format fails while others succeed for the identical report, the issue is specific to that format's rendering logic.
solution: Provide the customer an alternate format as an immediate workaround, and fix the format-specific rendering or size limitation.
escalation: Escalate if a specific export format is confirmed broken and requires a rendering-logic fix.

title: Incorrect Report Data
identifier: Report totals/values do not match the customer's own source data
problem: A report generates and downloads successfully, but the data within it does not match what the customer expects based on their own records.
visual: Report totals/values do not match the customer's own source data
Report totals highlighted next to the customer's own source data for comparison
Two versions of the same report from different dates showing inconsistent totals
Filter panel screenshot showing filters that may not match customer intent
symptoms: Report totals or values differ from the customer's own records.
Data appears to be missing rows or includes unexpected entries.
Discrepancy appeared after a recent change to the report or data source.
causes: A timezone mismatch is affecting how date-based data is grouped.
Report filters are not being applied as the customer expects.
The underlying data sync has a delay, so recent data is missing.
A calculation or aggregation error exists in the report logic.
steps: Compare the report's filters against what the customer intended to apply.
Check for a timezone setting mismatch affecting date grouping.
Confirm whether the underlying data sync is current or delayed.
Regenerate the report and compare against a manual data check.
Isolate whether the discrepancy is consistent or specific to certain rows.
decision: If the discrepancy is a consistent offset (e.g., always off by one day), suspect timezone handling; if it's inconsistent, suspect an aggregation bug.
solution: Correct the timezone or filter setting causing the mismatch, or explain the data sync delay to the customer, then confirm the regenerated report matches expectations.
escalation: Escalate if the report logic itself appears to be calculating values incorrectly, since this requires a code-level fix.

title: Scheduled Report Failure
identifier: A scheduled report does not arrive at its configured time
problem: A report that is scheduled to run and deliver automatically fails to arrive on its expected schedule.
visual: A scheduled report does not arrive at its configured time
Schedule settings screen showing the configured time and recipients
Delivery log showing no execution at the scheduled time
Email inbox with no scheduled report present at the expected time
symptoms: The scheduled report does not arrive at its configured time.
No error is visible to the customer; the report simply doesn't appear.
May happen once or on every scheduled occurrence.
causes: The scheduling job itself failed to trigger.
The report's recipient list or delivery email is misconfigured.
A timezone mismatch causes the report to run at an unexpected time.
The report generation step failed silently before delivery could occur.
steps: Check the scheduling system's logs for whether the job triggered at all.
Confirm the configured recipient list and delivery email are correct.
Check the account's timezone setting against the scheduled time.
Check whether report generation itself failed before the delivery step.
Manually trigger the scheduled report as a test.
decision: If the schedule never triggers at all, focus on the scheduling engine; if it triggers but generation fails, treat as a REP-001 style issue.
solution: Correct the schedule configuration, recipient list, or timezone setting, then confirm the next scheduled run delivers successfully.
escalation: Escalate if the scheduling job is confirmed not triggering at all, which may indicate a scheduler-service defect.

title: Workflow or Automation Not Triggering
identifier: An automation/workflow does not run when its trigger condition is met
problem: A customer has configured an automated workflow (trigger-action rule) that does not run when its trigger condition is met.
visual: An automation/workflow does not run when its trigger condition is met
Workflow builder screenshot showing the trigger and action configuration
Activity log showing no execution entries despite the trigger event occurring
Comparison of a working vs. non-working workflow's settings
symptoms: The workflow's expected action never occurs despite the trigger condition being met.
No error message is shown to the customer; the automation is simply silent.
Other workflows on the same account may be functioning normally.
causes: The trigger condition is configured more narrowly than the customer intends.
The workflow was accidentally disabled or paused.
A permission issue is preventing the workflow's action step from executing.
The workflow engine is experiencing a processing delay or backlog.
steps: Confirm the workflow is enabled/active, not paused or disabled.
Review the exact trigger condition configuration for narrowness or mismatch.
Check the workflow's execution log for any attempted but failed runs.
Confirm the workflow has permission to perform its configured action.
Manually trigger a test event to confirm whether the workflow fires.
decision: If the execution log shows zero attempts at all, the trigger condition itself isn't matching; if it shows failed attempts, the action step is the problem.
solution: Correct the trigger condition, re-enable the workflow, or resolve the permission blocking the action, then confirm a test trigger fires successfully.
escalation: Escalate if the workflow engine shows a processing backlog affecting multiple customers' automations.
related: COMP-008 (Webhook Received but Business Action Does Not Occur)

title: Feature Works for One User but Not Another
identifier: Identical feature works for User A but fails for User B on the same account
problem: The exact same feature functions correctly for one user in an organization but fails or behaves differently for another user in the same account.
visual: Identical feature works for User A but fails for User B on the same account
Two screenshots side-by-side: same feature, same account, different users, different results
Role/permission comparison screenshot for both users
Browser console showing an error only under one user's session
symptoms: One user reports the feature works; another on the same account reports it fails.
Both users are on the same account/organization and plan.
No account-wide outage is occurring since other users are unaffected.
causes: The two users have different roles or permission sets.
Individual user-level settings or preferences differ.
One user's session/cache is in a different state than the other's.
A user-specific data condition (e.g., missing profile field) affects only one of them.
steps: Compare both users' roles and permissions side-by-side.
Compare individual account settings and preferences between the two users.
Ask the affected user to clear cache/cookies and retry in a fresh session.
Check for any user-specific data condition unique to the failing user.
Attempt to reproduce the failure using a test account configured identically to the affected user.
decision: If a role, permission, or setting difference is found, correct it directly. If both users are configured identically and one still fails, escalate for application-level investigation.
solution: Align the failing user's role, settings, or data condition to match the working user, and confirm the feature now works for both.
escalation: Escalate if both users are confirmed to have identical configurations yet one consistently fails.

title: API Works for Some Requests but Fails for Others
identifier: Some API requests to the same endpoint succeed while others fail
problem: A customer's integration sees some API requests succeed while functionally similar requests to the same endpoint fail.
visual: Some API requests to the same endpoint succeed while others fail
Two API logs side-by-side: identical endpoint, different payloads, different results
Response comparison showing success (200) vs. failure (4xx/5xx) for similar calls
Highlighted diff between a working and failing request payload
symptoms: Some requests to an endpoint succeed while others of the same type fail.
The failure isn't tied to a full outage, since most requests work.
Failing requests may share a specific characteristic (payload size, field value, timing).
causes: A specific field value or payload structure in the failing requests triggers an edge case.
Rate limiting is affecting only requests that exceed a threshold.
The failing requests target a specific resource with a data-level issue.
Timing-related race conditions affect only certain request sequences.
steps: Collect several examples of both successful and failing requests.
Diff the payloads to identify what's different about the failing ones.
Check whether failing requests are hitting a specific resource ID or rate limit.
Check timing/sequence: are failing requests submitted in rapid succession?
Test the exact failing payload in isolation to confirm it reproduces the failure.
decision: Once a specific differentiating factor is identified (a field value, a resource, a rate threshold), the fix is targeted; if no pattern emerges, escalate for deeper log analysis.
solution: Fix the edge case in the differentiating factor (e.g., handle the specific field value correctly, adjust rate limit awareness), then confirm all request variants succeed.
escalation: Escalate if no consistent pattern can be identified between successful and failing requests after payload comparison.

title: Integration Stops After Credential Rotation
identifier: Integration fails immediately after an API credential was rotated
problem: A customer's integration was working normally but stopped functioning immediately after they rotated (regenerated) their API credentials.
visual: Integration fails immediately after an API credential was rotated
Old vs. new API key/token screenshot from the customer's integration settings
Error log showing authentication failures starting exactly at the rotation timestamp
Integration status showing "Disconnected" right after the customer's credential update
symptoms: Integration failure begins at the exact time credentials were rotated.
The customer confirms they updated the credential recently.
The integration was functioning normally immediately before the rotation.
causes: The new credential was not fully propagated to all parts of the customer's integration.
The new credential has different scopes/permissions than the old one.
The customer updated the credential in one place but missed a secondary configuration.
A caching layer is still using the old, now-invalid credential.
steps: Confirm the exact timestamp of the credential rotation versus when failures began.
Check whether the new credential has the same scopes as the old one.
Ask the customer to confirm the new credential was updated in all relevant places.
Check for any caching layer that might still hold the old credential.
Test the new credential directly to confirm it is valid and correctly scoped.
decision: If the new credential is valid and correctly scoped but the integration still fails, look for a caching or propagation delay rather than a customer configuration mistake.
solution: Update the credential everywhere it's referenced, clear any stale cache, and confirm the integration resumes normal operation.
escalation: Escalate if the new credential is confirmed valid and fully propagated but the integration still fails.

title: Data Synchronization Partially Fails
identifier: Sync job reports "completed" but record counts don't match between systems
problem: A sync process between two systems completes, but only part of the expected data is transferred, with some records silently missing.
visual: Sync job reports "completed" but record counts don't match between systems
Sync summary showing 'X of Y records synced' with a gap
Side-by-side record count comparison between source and destination systems
Sync log showing specific failed record entries rather than a total failure
symptoms: The sync job reports as 'completed' but record counts don't match between systems.
Some records transfer correctly while others are silently skipped.
No obvious error is shown since the job technically 'succeeded'.
causes: Specific records fail validation and are silently skipped rather than erroring out.
A pagination or batching bug causes some pages of records to be missed.
Certain records contain data that doesn't map cleanly between the two systems' schemas.
A rate limit is causing some records to be dropped mid-sync without retry.
steps: Compare total record counts between source and destination systems.
Check the sync log specifically for skipped or silently failed record entries.
Identify what's different about the missing records versus the successfully synced ones.
Check for pagination/batching logic that could be dropping certain pages.
Manually re-sync just the missing records as a targeted test.
decision: A 'completed' status with a count mismatch is a bigger red flag than an outright failure — it means the sync process needs stronger validation and error reporting, not just a retry.
solution: Fix the specific mapping, batching, or validation issue causing records to be silently dropped, then confirm a full sync produces matching record counts.
escalation: Escalate whenever a sync reports success but record counts don't match, since this indicates a silent data-integrity risk.

title: Dashboard Fails for Multiple Users
identifier: Multiple unrelated customers report dashboard failures at the same time
problem: Multiple customers, not just one, report their dashboards failing to load or displaying errors around the same time.
visual: Multiple unrelated customers report dashboard failures at the same time
Multiple customers' screenshots showing the same or similar dashboard error
Service health monitoring dashboard showing degraded status for a dashboard-related service
Support queue showing a cluster of similar tickets arriving in a short window
symptoms: Several unrelated customers report the same dashboard issue in a short time window.
The issue is not isolated to one account's data or configuration.
May correlate with a recent deployment or infrastructure event.
causes: A backend service that powers dashboards for all customers is degraded.
A recent deployment introduced a regression affecting a shared component.
A shared dependency (database, cache layer) is experiencing issues.
Increased load is causing dashboard queries to time out broadly.
steps: Confirm whether this is affecting multiple customers simultaneously (check support queue volume).
Check the health/status of shared backend services powering dashboards.
Check whether a deployment occurred shortly before reports began.
Check infrastructure metrics (load, database performance) for signs of strain.
Communicate a known-issue status internally so other tickets can reference it.
decision: Multiple simultaneous reports of the same symptom is itself the signal to treat this as an incident, not a series of individual tickets — escalate immediately rather than troubleshooting each ticket independently.
solution: Resolve the underlying shared service, deployment regression, or infrastructure strain, then confirm dashboards recover for all affected customers.
escalation: Escalate immediately as a potential incident whenever multiple customers report the same dashboard symptom in a short window.
related: COMP-006 (Application Becomes Slow for Multiple Users)

title: Application Becomes Slow for Multiple Users
identifier: Multiple unrelated customers report general application slowness at the same time
problem: Multiple customers report the application becoming noticeably slower than usual across various features, not tied to a single page or action.
visual: Multiple unrelated customers report general application slowness at the same time
Multiple customers' screen recordings showing long load times across different pages
Infrastructure monitoring graph showing elevated response times or resource usage
Support queue showing a spike in 'slow' complaints across accounts
symptoms: Several customers report general slowness rather than one specific error.
Slowness may affect multiple unrelated features simultaneously.
Often correlates with a specific time window or usage spike.
causes: Increased overall traffic/load is straining shared infrastructure.
A specific slow database query is affecting shared resources for all customers.
A recent deployment introduced a performance regression.
A shared dependency (cache, queue, third-party service) is degraded, causing cascading slowness.
steps: Confirm whether slowness is broad (multiple features/customers) or narrow (one feature/customer).
Check infrastructure metrics for elevated load, CPU, or database response time.
Check whether a deployment occurred around when slowness began.
Identify any specific slow database query or shared dependency causing strain.
Communicate a known-issue status internally while root cause is investigated.
decision: Broad, multi-customer slowness is an infrastructure/performance incident, not something resolvable through individual account troubleshooting — treat as an incident immediately.
solution: Resolve the underlying infrastructure strain, slow query, or deployment regression, then confirm response times return to normal for affected customers.
escalation: Escalate immediately as a potential incident whenever slowness is reported by multiple unrelated customers.

title: SSO Works for Some Users but Not Others
identifier: SSO login succeeds for some users in an org but fails for others
problem: Within a single organization using Single Sign-On, some users can authenticate successfully while others cannot, despite using the same SSO configuration.
visual: SSO login succeeds for some users in an org but fails for others
Two users' SSO login attempts side-by-side: one succeeding, one failing
Identity provider user-provisioning screen showing a difference between the two users
SSO error code specific to the failing user only
symptoms: Some users in the organization log in via SSO successfully.
Other users in the same organization fail to authenticate via the same SSO setup.
The SSO configuration itself is confirmed active and working for at least some users.
causes: The failing users are not correctly provisioned in the identity provider.
The failing users' email addresses don't match between the IdP and the platform.
A group/role assignment in the IdP excludes the failing users from SSO access.
The failing users have a stale or conflicting local account preventing SSO linkage.
steps: Confirm which specific users are failing versus succeeding.
Check the failing users' provisioning status and group assignment in the IdP.
Compare the failing users' email address in the IdP against their platform account.
Check for a pre-existing local account that might conflict with SSO linkage for the failing users.
Correct provisioning/email mismatch and retest login for the failing users.
decision: Since the SSO configuration itself clearly works (other users succeed), focus entirely on the failing users' individual provisioning rather than the SSO setup.
solution: Correct the failing users' provisioning, group assignment, or email mismatch in the IdP, then confirm they can log in successfully.
escalation: Escalate if provisioning and email matching are confirmed correct for the failing users but SSO login still fails.
related: COMP-001 (Feature Works for One User but Not Another)

title: Webhook Received but Business Action Does Not Occur
identifier: Webhook delivery log shows "200 OK" received but no resulting action occurred
problem: A webhook event is confirmed to have been received by the platform, but the expected downstream action (e.g., updating a record, sending a notification) never happens.
visual: Webhook delivery log shows "200 OK" received but no resulting action occurred
Webhook delivery log showing 'Received: 200 OK' but no corresponding action in the activity log
Timeline comparison: webhook timestamp vs. missing action timestamp
Processing queue screenshot showing the webhook event stuck or dropped
symptoms: The webhook delivery log confirms the event was received successfully.
The expected downstream business action (update, notification, record change) never occurs.
No error is shown since the webhook receipt itself succeeded.
causes: The webhook payload is received but fails silently during internal processing.
A specific field in the payload doesn't match what the processing logic expects.
The event is queued for processing but the processing worker is stuck or backlogged.
A duplicate-event guard is incorrectly treating this as an already-processed event.
steps: Confirm the webhook was received successfully (200 response) in the delivery log.
Check the internal processing queue/log for what happened to the event after receipt.
Compare the received payload structure against what the processing logic expects.
Check for a duplicate-event guard that might be incorrectly suppressing this event.
Manually reprocess the specific webhook event as a test.
decision: A successfully received but silently unprocessed webhook is a processing-logic gap, not a delivery problem — do not focus troubleshooting on the webhook connection itself.
solution: Fix the payload-matching or duplicate-detection logic causing the silent failure, then confirm the business action completes for a fresh test event.
escalation: Escalate whenever a webhook is confirmed received but consistently produces no downstream action, since this requires an engineering-level processing fix.
related: BILL-002 (Payment Successful but Access Not Updated)

title: Integration Works in Test but Fails in Production
identifier: Integration succeeds in sandbox/test but fails when pointed at production
problem: A customer's integration functions correctly in a test/sandbox environment but fails when pointed at the production environment.
visual: Integration succeeds in sandbox/test but fails when pointed at production
Side-by-side configuration comparison: test environment vs. production environment settings
Environment-specific error only appearing in the production request log
URL/endpoint screenshot showing which environment is being targeted
symptoms: The exact same integration logic succeeds in test/sandbox mode.
The same logic fails when switched to point at production.
The customer confirms no code changes were made between environments, only the target.
causes: Production credentials differ from test credentials and were not updated correctly.
Production has stricter rate limits or validation rules than the test environment.
A production-only feature flag or permission is not enabled for the customer's account.
The production endpoint URL differs from the test URL and wasn't updated.
steps: Confirm the customer updated all environment-specific values (URL, credentials, IDs) for production.
Compare rate limits and validation rules between test and production for this account.
Check whether the required feature/permission is enabled on the production account.
Test the exact same payload manually against the production endpoint to isolate the failure.
Review production-specific logs for the exact error at the time of the customer's attempt.
decision: Since test succeeds, the integration logic itself is sound — focus exclusively on what differs between the two environments rather than the customer's code.
solution: Correct the environment-specific configuration difference (credentials, URL, feature flag, rate limit) and confirm production now behaves like test.
escalation: Escalate if all environment-specific configuration is confirmed matching and production still fails while test succeeds.
related: COMP-002 (API Works for Some Requests but Fails for Others)

title: Same Problem Returns After Resolution
identifier: A previously closed/resolved ticket's exact symptom has reoccurred
