problem: An issue that was previously resolved and confirmed fixed for a customer has reoccurred, either immediately or after some time has passed.
visual: A previously closed/resolved ticket's exact symptom has reoccurred
Ticket history screenshot showing a previous resolved ticket for the identical symptom
Timeline showing the gap between resolution and recurrence
Comparison of the customer's current state versus what was configured at time of original fix
symptoms: The customer reports the exact same symptom as a previously closed ticket.
The original fix was confirmed working at the time it was closed.
Recurrence may be immediate or may happen after a delay.
causes: The original fix addressed the symptom but not the true root cause.
A subsequent change (deployment, configuration edit) undid the original fix.
The underlying condition that caused the issue was temporary and has now recurred.
A different, similar-looking issue is being mistaken for the same root cause.
steps: Pull the original ticket and confirm exactly what fix was applied previously.
Check whether anything has changed on the account or platform since the original fix.
Confirm whether the current symptom is truly identical or only superficially similar.
Determine whether the original fix treated a symptom rather than the root cause.
If the root cause was never fixed, treat this ticket as an opportunity to fix it properly.
decision: A recurrence is a strong signal that the original resolution was a workaround rather than a true fix — treat this as a priority for root-cause escalation rather than repeating the same workaround.
solution: Apply a root-cause fix this time rather than repeating the previous workaround, and confirm the issue does not recur after a reasonable monitoring period.
escalation: Escalate any recurring issue directly to engineering with the full history of the original ticket and fix attached.
related: COMP-001 (Feature Works for One User but Not Another)
COMP-015 (No Known Solution in Knowledge Base)

title: Payment Successful but Subscription Webhook Fails
identifier: Payment succeeded but the subscription-status webhook never updated the account
problem: A customer's payment is processed successfully by the payment provider, but the webhook that should notify the platform of this success fails to update the subscription status.
visual: Payment succeeded but the subscription-status webhook never updated the account
Payment provider dashboard showing 'Succeeded' status for the charge
Webhook delivery log showing a failed or missing delivery attempt for this event
Account subscription status still showing 'Inactive' or 'Past Due' despite successful payment
symptoms: Payment is confirmed successful directly in the payment provider's dashboard.
The platform's subscription status does not reflect the successful payment.
No webhook delivery is recorded for this payment event, or it shows as failed.
causes: The webhook endpoint was temporarily unreachable when the event was sent.
The webhook payload signature validation failed, causing it to be rejected.
The webhook was delivered but processing failed silently on receipt.
The payment event and the customer's account were not correctly linked.
steps: Confirm the payment status directly in the payment provider's dashboard.
Check the webhook delivery log for this specific event's delivery attempt and result.
If delivery failed, check whether the endpoint was reachable at that time.
If delivered but not processed, check internal processing logs for a silent failure.
Manually update the subscription status to unblock the customer, then fix the webhook issue.
decision: Always unblock the customer's access manually first once payment is verified, then investigate the webhook failure separately — don't make the customer wait on the root-cause investigation.
solution: Manually apply the correct subscription status immediately, then fix the underlying webhook delivery or signature validation issue to prevent recurrence.
escalation: Escalate to engineering if webhook delivery failures for payment events are recurring rather than a single incident.
related: BILL-002 (Payment Successful but Access Not Updated)
COMP-008 (Webhook Received but Business Action Does Not Occur)

title: Report Data Differs From Source System
identifier: Platform report figures differ from the customer's own source-of-truth system
problem: A report generated by the platform shows different figures than the customer's own source-of-truth system for the same underlying data.
visual: Platform report figures differ from the customer's own source-of-truth system
Side-by-side numbers: platform report total vs. source system total
Highlighted specific rows/records that differ between the two systems
Timestamp comparison showing when each system's data was last updated
symptoms: The customer has an independent source system they trust as ground truth.
The platform's report shows a different total or set of records than that source.
The discrepancy may be small (rounding/timing) or large (missing data).
causes: A sync delay means the platform's data is not yet current with the source system.
The two systems calculate the same metric using different logic or filters.
A timezone or date-boundary difference causes records to be grouped differently.
Some records failed to sync from the source system and are simply missing.
steps: Confirm exactly which figures differ and by how much.
Check the last sync timestamp between the platform and the source system.
Compare the calculation logic/filters used by each system for this metric.
Check for a timezone or date-boundary difference affecting grouping.
Identify whether specific records are entirely missing versus just calculated differently.
decision: A small, consistent discrepancy usually points to timezone or calculation logic differences; a large or growing gap points to a sync failure with missing records.
solution: Correct the sync delay, align calculation logic between systems, or fix the timezone handling, then confirm the platform's report matches the source system.
escalation: Escalate if the discrepancy is confirmed to stem from missing synced records or a calculation-logic bug rather than expected timing differences.

title: Notifications Work for Some Users but Not Others
identifier: Some users on an account receive a notification type while others do not
problem: Within the same account, some users receive a specific notification type reliably while other users on the same account do not.
visual: Some users on an account receive a notification type while others do not
Two users' notification preference screens side-by-side showing a difference
Notification delivery log showing success for one user, failure/skip for another
Email address or device-token comparison between the two users
symptoms: Some users on the account receive the notification consistently.
Other users on the same account, for the same event type, do not.
The account-level notification configuration is confirmed enabled.
causes: The affected users have the specific notification type disabled individually.
The affected users' contact info (email/device token) is outdated or invalid.
A per-user permission or subscription setting excludes them from this notification.
The affected users' notification delivery is being blocked by their own email/device settings.
steps: Confirm the account-level notification setting is enabled (ruling out a account-wide config issue).
Compare the affected users' individual notification preferences against working users.
Confirm the affected users' email address or device token is current and valid.
Check for a per-user permission or subscription flag that could exclude them.
Send a manual test notification directly to an affected user to confirm delivery.
decision: Since other users receive it fine, the account-level configuration is not the problem — investigate only the affected users' individual settings and contact info.
solution: Correct the affected users' individual notification preference or contact info, then confirm they receive a test notification successfully.
escalation: Escalate if affected users' individual settings and contact info are all confirmed correct but they still don't receive notifications.
related: COMP-001 (Feature Works for One User but Not Another)

title: Feature Stops Working After Product Update
identifier: A feature stopped working immediately after a platform update/release
problem: A feature that was working normally stops functioning correctly immediately following a platform update or new release.
visual: A feature stopped working immediately after a platform update/release
Release notes screenshot for the update that coincides with the failure
Before/after screenshot comparing the feature's behavior pre- and post-update
Error appearing only in versions/builds after the update
symptoms: The feature worked correctly before a specific update and fails immediately after.
The timing of the failure closely matches a known release or deployment.
Other unrelated features may be unaffected, isolating the issue to this update.
causes: The update introduced a regression affecting this specific feature.
The update changed a dependency or API contract that this feature relies on.
A configuration migration during the update did not complete correctly for this account.
The update requires a new setting or permission that wasn't automatically applied.
steps: Confirm the exact timing of the failure against the release/deployment timeline.
Review the release notes for changes that could plausibly affect this feature.
Check whether a configuration migration ran successfully for the affected account.
Test the feature on an account that was not affected, if possible, to confirm the pattern.
Check whether a new setting or permission introduced by the update needs to be enabled.
decision: Precise timing correlation with a release is strong evidence of a regression — prioritize checking the release notes and rollback options before deep individual debugging.
solution: Apply a hotfix for the regression, complete the missed configuration migration, or enable the newly required setting, then confirm the feature works again.
escalation: Escalate immediately to engineering when a feature failure's timing closely matches a recent release, since a regression fix is likely required.

title: No Known Solution in Knowledge Base
identifier: Reported symptoms do not match any existing knowledge base guide
problem: A customer's issue does not match any existing troubleshooting guide, and no documented cause or fix currently exists for it.
visual: Reported symptoms do not match any existing knowledge base guide
Junior developer's search results showing no matching guide found
Screenshot of the unique/unfamiliar symptom the customer is describing
Ticket marked as 'Unclassified' or 'New Issue Type'
symptoms: The issue's symptoms do not clearly match any existing guide's problem statement.
Standard troubleshooting steps for similar-sounding issues do not resolve it.
This may be a genuinely new issue type not yet seen before.
causes: This is a newly emerging issue not yet documented in the knowledge base.
The issue is a rare edge case that hasn't been formally investigated.
The issue may be a variation of a known problem with an unusual trigger.
Insufficient information has been gathered yet to properly classify the issue.
steps: Gather the fullest possible detail: exact steps to reproduce, environment, timing, error text, and screenshots.
Search the knowledge base using different keyword combinations before concluding no match exists.
Check with a senior developer or team lead whether this issue has been seen informally before.
Document the issue thoroughly even if unresolved, to seed a future knowledge base entry.
Do not guess at a fix — clearly flag this as an unclassified issue when escalating.
decision: Never attempt to force-fit an unfamiliar issue into an existing guide's steps — misapplied troubleshooting can mask the real problem and waste the customer's time.
solution: There is no documented solution yet. The immediate goal is thorough documentation and escalation, not resolution at the junior developer level.
escalation: Escalate immediately with full documentation whenever no existing guide matches the reported symptoms.
related: COMP-014 (Feature Stops Working After Product Update)
